### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb05ea2fa15b5c6a91fc0664d3a13fe57a9433af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `890f76daa47cc4244b1805ac5c4bf2d2e6ac40cb` — the merge of head `542f0d8825d8a8e1d112168037eb9670ccd2cd14` into base `eb05ea2fa15b5c6a91fc0664d3a13fe57a9433af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 890f76daa47cc4244b1805ac5c4bf2d2e6ac40cb && git checkout 890f76daa47cc4244b1805ac5c4bf2d2e6ac40cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb05ea2fa15b5c6a91fc0664d3a13fe57a9433af 542f0d8825d8a8e1d112168037eb9670ccd2cd14 && git checkout -B drift-repro eb05ea2fa15b5c6a91fc0664d3a13fe57a9433af && git merge --no-ff 542f0d8825d8a8e1d112168037eb9670ccd2cd14

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb05ea2fa15b5c6a91fc0664d3a13fe57a9433af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `542f0d8825d8a8e1d112168037eb9670ccd2cd14`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/approvals-no-submitter-submitter-verbs.md + packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts (`IApprovalService.recall` / `resubmit`, `ApprovalRecallInput`, `ApprovalResubmitInput`), packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts (`approval_recall` / `approval_remind` / `approval_resubmit` visibility), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts (`runTriggerUser`), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (which triggers resolve no user), .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/lint.yml (the gates the dev's notes name)

Face: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; `record-recognisers --paths` reads no path face off the file list and defers to that line, so the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces, all listed above. The branch sits at merge-base `4ab2e7e66b`, 50 commits behind `main` at `a932270068`; none of those commits touch `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`, `packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts` or the spec contract, GitHub reports it mergeable and clean, so the diff still applies cleanly in meaning.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change on a request whose `submitter_id` is empty, FROM `main` at the merge-base TO this head, per caller class and door. On `main` the three doors tested "is the caller the submitter" only when the row named one, so a request with no submitter admitted every caller who could read it. The new `actsAsSubmitter` predicate answers no for every actor on such a row, and each door keeps its other arms as they were.

- **Pending approver** (reads through the slate): recall on `pending`, recall on `returned`, remind, resubmit — admitted → refused `FORBIDDEN`, the door's existing non-submitter sentence, nothing written. Pinned at the service (byte-equal to the refusal the same caller gets on a submitted request) and at the HTTP door (`403 FORBIDDEN`, request and history unchanged).
- **Record reader** (opt-in `recordReaderVisibleObjects` tier, same organization): same four — admitted → refused. The tier's own doc block says seeing a request confers nothing; these three doors now hold that.
- **Plain member** (cannot read it): `404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` before and after — `refuseUnreadableRequest` runs ahead of the submitter test at all three doors, unchanged.
- **Tenant admin** (override actor, judged against the request's organization): recall on `pending` — admitted → admitted (`overrideAdmits`). Recall on `returned`, remind, resubmit — admitted → refused. Those three never admitted the override: `IApprovalService.recall` and `ApprovalRecallInput` make `returned` the submitter's alone, and `remind` / `resubmit` carry no override arm. The declared actions agree: `approval_recall` ORs `viewer.can_override` (itself pending-only), `approval_remind` and `approval_resubmit` gate on `is_submitter` alone.
- **Platform admin**: as the tenant admin, crossing the organization wall on recall of a `pending` request as before; `isOverrideActor` is untouched.
- **System context**: recall on `pending`, remind, resubmit — admitted → admitted (`isSystem` arm at each door). Recall on `returned` — admitted → refused. Judged: not a narrowing nobody asked for. The contract text says in so many words that neither the override nor the system arm reaches a `returned` request, that it is the submitter's alone on the latest `returned` request of its run, and on `main` a system context IS already refused there on a request that has a submitter. The head aligns the no-submitter case with the published contract instead of carving an exception into it. Its operational consequence is in ③.
- **Cross-organization caller**: `404` before and after, the read wall unchanged. An org-scoped submitter on an org-less request: `404` on recall, remind, resubmit and comment, now pinned beside the approver case; no behaviour change.
- **A request that has a submitter**: unchanged in every class. With a non-empty submitter the predicate is the former comparison, and `resolveActor` never returns an empty actor (it throws or returns the caller's own id, or the explicit actor a system context must name), so no submitted request changes hands. Control tests pin submitter recall, remind and resubmit at both layers.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset present: `.changeset/approvals-no-submitter-submitter-verbs.md`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with a FROM / TO block, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a BREAKING banner, the title's `!`, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- Level: correct. A non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; nothing an author can write changes, so `none` and no D3 entry are right — no metadata is refused, no key, export or type moves.
- Nit, not blocking: the changeset's FROM line names only the readers who lose the doors; the override actor also loses remind, resubmit and returned-recall on such a request, and the system context loses returned-recall. The TO line is complete, so the reader can derive it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on the head**: every run is `completed`; none is still running. Required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and its eight shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` all `success`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` `skipped` by the path filter (no `ui/` change). Advisory: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness` `success`.
- **The dogfood pin is not measured on this head.** `Dogfood Regression Gate` reads `success` as the aggregate, but its three shards are `skipped` on a `pull_request` event by design in `ci.yml` (the full battery runs on `main`'s push and scheduled runs). So the new HTTP-door describe is evidence the tree carries, measured after merge, not a gate verdict here. The service-level describe did run under `Test Core`.
- **Dev note, dogfood header**: confirmed — `origin/main` already names `approval-service.test.ts` as the server half in that file's header; the diff adds a paragraph and corrects nothing. Answered.
- **Dev note, `check-plugin-teardown-shape` after an unshallow**: that gate runs in `lint.yml` (self-test then gate) inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, green on this head; the local exit 3 was a clone-depth artefact of the dev's checkout, not of the tree. Answered.
- **Dev note, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally**: `ci.yml` runs it in `Build Core`, green on this head. Answered. Nothing to escalate.
- **Consequence of the contract reading, for the maintainer's awareness, not a defect in this tree**: a request with no submitter that an approver sends back (`returned`) is now recallable by nobody — there is no submitter, and the contract refuses the system and override arms there — and its run waits at the revise node until a system context resubmits it (which opens a fresh `pending` round the override can recall). The record is unlocked while `returned`, so nothing is held. Whether `sendBack` should refuse a request nobody can rework is a contract question outside this PR.
- Not relied on: the PR body's ablation and suite accounts. The tree, its tests and the head's check-runs were the inputs.

### ④ Design judgment

- **No fourth door.** Every `submitter_id` read in `approval-service.ts` on the head was enumerated. The three doors are the only authorizing reads that admit a caller as the submitter. `comment` reads it to choose the submitter arm and otherwise falls through to the slot test, so with no submitter a caller off the slate is refused and a system context is admitted — fails closed, correctly left alone. Decide's `excludeSubmitter` check, `excludedSubmitterSlots` and `assertReassignTargetIsNotSubmitter` exclude a submitter from a slate; with none, nobody is excluded, which is right. `attachViewers.is_submitter` is false with no submitter and `can_override` is pending-only, so the declared actions and the server agree. The notification audiences, the inbox filter, the list filter and the display labels read the column for addressing and display, never for authorization. `sendBack`, `requestInfo` and `reassign` judge the slate or the override only.
- **REST**: `approvals-routes.ts` forwards the session context and the body's `actorId`, which `resolveActor` pins to an identity the caller provably holds; a REST caller never carries `isSystem`. The routes hold no submitter gate of their own, unchanged.
- **A user-less flow's own runtime**: no caller of `recall`, `remind` or `resubmit` exists in the tree outside the REST routes — the automation engine, the lifecycle hooks, the SLA sweep and the action-link handler do not call them. A run whose trigger resolved no user (schedule, time-relative, api, or a record write with no user) acts, when elevated, as a system context, and the system arms are kept. No legitimate non-system actor is cut off.
- **Org-scoped override actor**: `isOverrideActor` is unchanged — a tenant admin reaches only a request in their own organization or an org-less one, a platform admin crosses the wall, a system context passes — and it is still judged against the request's own `organization_id`. The tenant-admin pin runs in the request's organization.
- **Resubmit by the override**: never admitted by that door; on a no-submitter request it is now refused like any non-submitter, and pinned.
- **Predicate edges**: `null` and the empty string both read as "no submitter", so neither spelling of an empty column opens a door. `actorId` is never empty by the time the predicate runs. The developer-facing log line now says "no submitter" instead of printing a null id; its metadata object still stringifies the column (cosmetic).
- **The tests can fail**: they assert `FORBIDDEN` exactly where `main`'s tree admits, pin the refusal byte-equal to the with-submitter yardstick, and pin no-write by row and history snapshot. The dogfood describe opens the no-submitter request the way a user-less run really does (a system-context record write firing the record-change trigger) and asserts the column is empty before judging.
- No must-fix found.
